title: Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) Process Control Systems
description: This course covers Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) systems, function, interrelationship, and troubleshooting of systems components. PLC input/output systems and requirements are also discussed. Ladder logic programming is studied using basic I/O instructions, logic instructions, timers, counters, and comparison functions. Students will also develop an understanding of Piping/Process and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&ID).
outcomes: Describe the functions and operations of a process control system at the block level.
Implement and troubleshoot a basic functional control system using ladder-logic programming
Design a PLC program using ladder-logic or function block diagramming using P&ID
Read and understand automation symbols, including International Society of Automation (ISA) symbols
objectives: Describe the functions and operations of a process control system at the block level
Implement a basic functional control system using ladder-logic programming
Develop and execute a troubleshooting plan for process control systems.
Develop and design PLC program from Piping/Process and Instrumentation Diagram
content: Overview of programmable logic control (PLC) systems
Rising Edge and Falling Edge Detection
Create and understand electrical plans for simple process systems
lab: Introduction to logic control simulation software
Build and test a basic ladder logic circuit with simulation software
Build and test circuits with multiple PLC controller elements
Build and test circuits with multiple PLC input elements
Build and test circuits with multiple PLC output elements
Create control panel diagrams, loop drawings, and electrical interconnection diagrams
assignments: Students are expected to work on homework in order to learn the materials
Example: Develop and execute a troubleshooting plan for a malfunctioning PLC system.
Students use the concepts and technical skills learned in the class to analyze and solve practical problems.
Example: Program PLC controller for a specified operation using Piping/Process Instrumentation Diagram (P&ID).
Example: Consider the design components for a PLC-Controlled Water Filtration System for Underserved Communities
Students demonstrate their understanding of the materials with written PLC code.
Example: Describe the expected operation of a PLC system from a ladder logic diagram or function block diagram.
